chunks: And it is narrated from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: I take dirhams from a man, then I weigh them, then I distribute them, and some surplus of them remains in my hand.
He said: Did you not seek to give full measure accurately?
I said: Yes. He said: There is no harm.

key_terms.أُفَرِّقُهَا: I distribute them; apportioning or handing them out
key_terms.الدَّرَاهِمَ: dirhams; silver coins used in financial transactions
key_terms.الْوَفَاءَ: full fulfillment; giving what is due completely
key_terms.تَحَرَّى: sought carefully; strove to act with precision and care
key_terms.فَأَزِنُهَا: I weigh them; measuring the coins by weight
key_terms.فَضْلٌ: surplus; an extra amount left over
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is there any problem if a small surplus remains after accurately weighing and distributing dirhams?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding minor surplus that remains after weighing and distributing dirhams. If the person has genuinely sought accuracy and fulfillment in the transaction, then the remaining slight excess is not blameworthy and there is no harm in it.
